rationale: The previous convergence run did not exercise the intended 150 rounds: its loop breaks whenever the queue is empty and any node has decided, so it stopped long before the default 100-tick resend interval and could not distinguish a resend-interval lag from a real non-convergence. This successor raises the bound to 150 and breaks only when all five decided indices are equal (or the bound is hit), so ticking continues past the resend timeout. Both the agreement and converged_all predicates are retained.

experiment.revision_reason: The convergence loop's early break (queue empty and any node decided) prevented the intended number of ticks, so the 150-round bound was never reached. The successor breaks only when all decided indices are equal or the bound is exhausted, keeping the same randomized phase, seed, reconfigure step and comparisons.

scope.description: Same five-node lossy stress (seed 0xbe5466cf34e90c6c, reconfigure at 450, 20 percent loss), run id 12, with up to 150 fair-delivery rounds that stop only when all decided indices are equal.
assumptions: Fair delivery with ticks on every node exercises the documented resend messengers; a tick per node per round advances each node's logical clocks.
No snapshots, trimming or starting the next configuration.
excluded: Starting the next configuration, snapshots, flexible quorums, crash-restart and Byzantine participants.

experiment.prefix: Identical randomized phase to the reconfiguration runs, with run id 12. After the loop, run up to 150 fair-delivery rounds; each round delivers all queued messages, ticks every node, and delivers again; break only when the queue is empty and all five decided indices are equal. Emit the safety event with appended, delivered, dropped, divergences, progressed, regressions, reconfigured, converged_all and decided indices.

comparisons.description: Bounded convergence past the resend timeout: all nodes report the same decided index.
Agreement retained under the full convergence attempt.
